mainTopic: The end of רבי שמעון's conditional offering for a מצורע, and the questions of אגדה, בורות and דרך ארץ that the people of Alexandria asked רבי יהושע
overview: This amud first finishes a ברייתא about רבי שמעון's idea that a מצורע in doubt can bring an animal with a condition: an אשם if he needs one, and a שלמים if not. Because of the doubt, the animal follows the stricter rules of both offerings. The חכמים reject this, because it shortens the eating time of what may be a שלמים. The גמרא answers that שמואל agrees with רבי שמעון on one point only. Then come the questions the people of Alexandria asked רבי יהושע. In three questions of אגדה, he settles contradictions between פסוקים: it depends on תשובה, on whether the גזר דין has already been given, and on whether it was before or after שלמה married בת פרעה. In three questions of בורות, he rules that a pillar of salt and a living person do not make things טמא, and he puts off the question about the revived dead for the future. In the questions of דרך ארץ, he teaches that wisdom and wealth need both effort and תפילה, and the question about having sons continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The strict rules for the conditional offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes listing the rules for רבי שמעון's conditional offering. It follows the stricter rules of both an אשם and a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It must be slaughtered in the north, it needs blood placed on the thumb and big toe, it needs leaning of hands, wine libations, and waving of the breast and thigh, and it is eaten only by male כהנים for one day and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון. The animal might be an אשם or might be a שלמים, so it is handled with the strict rules of both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the אשם side come slaughtering in the north, the blood on the thumb and toe, and eating only by male כהנים for a day and a night. From the שלמים side come the libations and the waving of the breast and thigh. Since we don't know which offering it really is, every stricter rule is followed.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering in the northern part of the עזרה, as required for an אשם
Putting the blood on the right thumb, big toe and ear of the מצורע
Leaning one's hands on the animal's head before slaughter
Wine libations that come with certain offerings
The breast and thigh of a שלמים, which are waved and given to the כהן
Male כהנים, the only ones allowed to eat an אשם

phrases.english: its slaughter is in the north,
phrases.notes: We're starting in the middle of the ברייתא. 'Its' means the animal the מצורע brings on a condition: an אשם if he needs one, a שלמים if not.

phrases.english: and it requires placing blood on the thumb and big toe,
and leaning of hands, and libations, and waving,
and the breast and thigh,
and it is eaten by males of the priesthood
for a day and a night.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחִיטָתוֹ בַּצָּפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא about רבי שמעון's conditional offering, which began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A conditional אשם/שלמים is handled with the stricter rules of both offerings.

steps.title: The Rabbis reject רבי שמעון's condition
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים did not accept רבי שמעון's idea. If the animal is really a שלמים, cutting its eating time short wastes קדשים. This ending of the ברייתא stands as a difficulty for שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the חכמים did not agree with רבי שמעון, because he brings holy offerings into a situation where they are more likely to become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the חכמים disagreeing with רבי שמעון. The גמרא is using this ברייתא as a challenge to שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שלמים may normally be eaten for two days and the night between them. Under רבי שמעון's plan it may be eaten for only one day and night, so any meat left after that becomes disqualified for no good reason. The חכמים do not allow a plan that causes קדשים to be lost.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים did not agree with him
A situation that makes disqualification more likely

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: But the Rabbis did not agree with Rabbi Shimon,
because he brings sacrifices to a situation of disqualification!
phrases.notes: Literally 'to the house of disqualification.' A שלמים normally gets two days, so cutting it to one makes leftovers go bad sooner.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the חכמים's rejection, which completes the difficulty against שמואל
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's position, which seems to depend on רבי שמעון's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's view is rejected by the חכמים. So how can שמואל follow it?

steps.title: שמואל agrees with רבי שמעון on one point only
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל follows רבי שמעון on one point and disagrees with him on another.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like רבי שמעון in one matter and disagrees with him in one matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. He does not take on all of רבי שמעון's view, only one part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל agrees with רבי שמעון that the אשם is not what decides whether the מצורע brings the offerings of a rich man or a poor man. But he does not allow a condition on an אשם, so the חכמים's objection does not hurt him.
steps.whatToRemember: You can follow a תנא on one point and still reject another point of his. Then an objection to the second point does not touch you.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: Shmuel holds like Rabbi Shimon in one matter,
phrases.notes: That one matter: the אשם doesn't decide whether he brings the rich man's or the poor man's offerings.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him in one matter.
phrases.notes: He disagrees about putting a condition on an אשם, so the חכמים's objection doesn't hurt him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty from the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the opinion: שמואל accepts only part of רבי שמעון's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed to follow רבי שמעון completely, including the condition the חכמים rejected
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי שמעון only on the rich/poor point and does not accept the condition on an אשם

steps.title: Two פסוקים contradict about the death of the wicked
steps.stepSummary: A new section opens: the three questions of אגדה. The first points out a contradiction. One פסוק says ה׳ does not want the death of the one who dies, and another says ה׳ wanted to kill the sons of עלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three matters of אגדה: One פסוק says, 'For I do not desire the death of the one who dies,' and another פסוק says, 'For ה׳ desired to kill them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the הלכה questions to the three אגדה questions the people of Alexandria asked רבי יהושע. The first one sets two פסוקים against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יחזקאל, ה׳ says He has no wish for anyone to die. But in שמואל, the sons of עלי did not listen to their father because ה׳ wanted to kill them. These look like opposite statements about what ה׳ wants.

keyTerms.meaning: Matters of אגדה, meaning non-legal Torah teachings
One פסוק says (the opening of a contradiction between פסוקים)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a הלכה here. This is a completely new topic, a question of אגדה, not a continuation of the קרבנות discussion.

phrases.english: Three matters of aggada:
One verse says
"For I do not desire the death of the one who dies",
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 18:32

phrases.english: and another verse says
"For the Lord desired to kill them"!
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:25, about the sons of עלי.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דִּבְרֵי אַגָּדָה כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, the אגדה questions, after the הלכה questions end
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים in יחזקאל and שמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says ה׳ does not want the wicked to die, and the other says He did want it.

steps.title: It depends on whether they do תשובה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: יחזקאל speaks about people who do תשובה, and שמואל speaks about people who do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it means those who do תשובה, and there it means those who do not do תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע settles the contradiction by showing that each פסוק describes a different kind of person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ does not want the death of a sinner who returns to Him. The sons of עלי refused to do תשובה, so for them death was what ה׳ wanted. The two פסוקים are not in conflict, because they describe different situations.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there; one source speaks about one case and the other about a different case

steps.whatToRemember: The way to settle these two פסוקים is תשובה. ה׳ does not want the death of one who repents, but someone who refuses to repent is a different case.

phrases.english: Here, it is where they repent,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the פסוק in יחזקאל.

phrases.english: there, it is where they do not repent.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the פסוק about the sons of עלי.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן בְּעוֹשִׂין תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in the previous step
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each פסוק refers to a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to give opposite accounts of what ה׳ wants
steps.terutzMaskana: יחזקאל speaks about those who repent, and שמואל about those who do not

steps.title: Does ה׳ show favor or not?
steps.stepSummary: A second contradiction in אגדה: one פסוק says ה׳ does not show favor, and another says ה׳ will show favor to you.
steps.simpleTranslation: One verse says: 'For He does not show favor and does not take a bribe.' Another verse says: 'May ה׳ lift His face toward you.' Which is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another question of אגדה. Two פסוקים seem to say opposite things about whether ה׳ shows favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ספר דברים, ה׳ is described as a judge who never 'lifts the face' (shows favor) of anyone. Yet in ברכת כהנים we ask that ה׳ 'lift His face' toward us. The same words are said 'no' in one place and 'yes' in the other.

keyTerms.meaning: One verse says (the opening of a contradiction between two פסוקים)
Lifts the face, meaning shows favor or special kindness

phrases.english: One verse says:
'For He does not show favor'
phrases.notes: דברים 10:17

phrases.english: 'and does not take a bribe'
And another verse says:
'May ה׳ lift His face toward you'!
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:26, from ברכת כהנים. 'Lift His face' here means show you favor.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר וְכָתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second contradiction in the series of אגדה questions that began in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: How the two פסוקים about ה׳ showing favor can both be true
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דברים says ה׳ never shows favor, while ברכת כהנים asks that He show favor. The two seem to cancel each other out.

steps.title: Before the verdict versus after the verdict
steps.stepSummary: The answer: ה׳ shows favor before the גזר דין is sealed, but not after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it means before the verdict is given; there it means after the verdict is given.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע settles the contradiction by saying each פסוק speaks about a different time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before a person's judgment is final, ה׳ can show favor and forgive, and that is the time ברכת כהנים is speaking about. Once the גזר דין has been given, ה׳ no longer 'lifts the face', and that is what the פסוק in דברים means. So both פסוקים are true, each at its own time.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there (splitting two sources into two different cases)

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that a person can still change his judgment through prayer and תשובה, as long as the verdict is not yet sealed.

phrases.english: Here, it is before the verdict;
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק of ברכת כהנים, where ה׳ shows favor.

phrases.english: there, it is after the verdict.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן קוֹדֶם גְּזַר דִּין, כָּאן לְאַחַר גְּזַר דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time: each פסוק applies at a different stage of judgment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים describe the same moment and flatly contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳ shows favor before the גזר דין and does not show favor after it

steps.title: Was ציון chosen, or was it always a cause of anger?
steps.stepSummary: A third contradiction: one פסוק says ה׳ chose ציון, and another says the city made Him angry from the day it was built.
steps.simpleTranslation: One verse says: 'For ה׳ has chosen ציון.' Another verse says: 'This city has made Me angry and furious from the day they built it until this day.' Which is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another contradiction between פסוקים, this time about ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תהלים says ה׳ chose ציון as His home. ירמיהו says the city angered ה׳ from the day it was built. The second פסוק seems to say the city was never loved.

phrases.english: One verse says
'For ה׳ has chosen ציון'
phrases.notes: תהלים 132:13

phrases.english: And another verse says
'For a cause of My anger and My fury'
'this city has been to Me'
'from the day that they built it'
'until this day'!
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 32:31

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״כִּי בָחַר ה׳ בְּצִיּוֹן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another contradiction question in the same series of אגדה questions
steps.kashyaTarget: How ציון can be both chosen by ה׳ and a cause of His anger from the day it was built
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the city angered ה׳ from its very first day, when was it ever chosen?

steps.title: Before and after שלמה married בת פרעה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: ציון was chosen until שלמה married בת פרעה. From then on it became a cause of anger.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it means before שלמה married בת פרעה; there it means after שלמה married בת פרעה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע again settles the contradiction by placing each פסוק in a different time period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer ties the change to one event: שלמה marrying בת פרעה. The פסוק in תהלים describes ציון before that marriage, when it was the chosen city. The פסוק in ירמיהו describes it after the marriage, when the city became a cause of anger.
steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions in this section (steps 6–9) are answered the same way: each פסוק is true, but at a different time.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן קוֹדֶם שֶׁנָּשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה,
phrases.english: Here, it is before שלמה married Pharaoh's daughter;

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן לְאַחַר שֶׁנָּשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה.
phrases.english: there, it is after שלמה married Pharaoh's daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן קוֹדֶם שֶׁנָּשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים describe ציון in the same period and contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: ציון was chosen before שלמה married בת פרעה, and became a cause of anger after that

steps.title: Does the wife of לוט make things impure?
steps.stepSummary: A new set opens: the three questions of בורות. The first asks whether the wife of לוט, who became a pillar of salt, gives off טומאת מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three foolish questions: What about the wife of לוט? Does she make things impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new group of questions, called 'questions of בורות', and brings the first one: does the wife of לוט give off טומאה like a dead body?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife of לוט was a person who turned into a pillar of salt. The question is whether that pillar counts as a dead body (מת) and so gives off טומאה. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Matters of ignorance: odd or foolish-sounding questions
What is the law, does it...?
The impurity given off by a dead body

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier 'questions of אגדה'. This is a new group, the questions of בורות, and they are about טומאה.

phrases.english: Three matters of ignorance:
Lot's wife,
does she make things impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דִּבְרֵי בּוּרוּת: אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל לוֹט, מַהוּ שֶׁתְּטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the questions of אגדה and opens the questions of בורות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person who became a pillar of salt gives off טומאת מת

steps.title: A pillar of salt is not a dead body
steps.stepSummary: The answer: only a dead body gives off טומאה, and a pillar of salt does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: A dead body makes things impure, but a pillar of salt does not make things impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is given: Lot's wife does not make things טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאה comes from a מת, a dead human body. The wife of לוט is no longer a body at all. She is now salt, so the laws of טומאת מת do not apply to her.

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהושע, who answers this whole series of questions.

phrases.english: A dead body makes impure,
but a pillar of salt does not make impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת מְטַמֵּא, וְאֵין נְצִיב מֶלַח מְטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wife of לוט does not make things טמא, because only a מת gives off טומאה and she is now salt

steps.title: Does the son of the שונמית make things impure?
steps.stepSummary: The second question of בורות: does the boy who died and was brought back to life by אלישע give off טומאת מת?
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the son of the Shunammite woman? Does he make things impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second question of בורות, about a boy who was once dead and then came back to life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son of the שונמית was truly dead for a while before אלישע brought him back to life. The question is whether having been a מת leaves him with טומאה even now that he is alive.

keyTerms.meaning: The son of the woman from שונם, whom אלישע brought back to life

phrases.english: The son of the Shunammite woman,
does he make things impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן שׁוּנַמִּית, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second question in the series of בורות questions
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether someone who died and came back to life still gives off טומאת מת

steps.title: A living person is not a dead body
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a living person does not make things טמא, even if he was once dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: A dead body makes things impure, but a living person does not make things impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is given: the boy does not make things טמא, because he is alive now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is his status right now. Since he is alive, he is not a מת, so he gives off no טומאת מת, even though he was dead for a while.
steps.whatToRemember: Both answers follow one rule: only an actual dead human body gives off טומאת מת. Salt that was once a person does not, and a living person who was once dead does not.

phrases.english: He said to them:
A dead body makes impure,
but a living person does not make impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת מְטַמֵּא, וְאֵין חַי מְטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12, using the same pattern as step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The son of the שונמית does not make things טמא, because he is alive and only a מת gives off טומאה

steps.title: Will the dead need sprinkling when they come back to life?
steps.stepSummary: The third question of בורות: will the dead who are revived in the future need the third-day and seventh-day sprinkling of טהרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: The dead in the time to come: will they need sprinkling on the third and seventh days, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The people of Alexandria ask their third question of בורות. When the dead come back to life in the future, will they need the הזאה on day three and day seven to become טהור?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who touched a dead body needs the הזאה of the ashes of the פרה אדומה on the third and seventh days. A revived person was once a dead body himself, so maybe he needs it too. This follows the pattern of the last two questions, which also asked about strange cases of death and טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: In the time to come, when the dead will come back to life
Sprinkling of the ashes of the פרה אדומה to remove טומאת מת
The third and seventh days of the purification process

phrases.english: The dead in the time to come,
do they need sprinkling on the third and seventh days
or do they not need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִים לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, צְרִיכִין הַזָּאָה שְׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי אוֹ אֵין צְרִיכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and last of the questions of בורות, after the wife of לוט and the boy revived by אלישע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether people revived at תחיית המתים need the הזאה used to remove טומאת מת.

steps.title: We will figure it out when it happens
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע puts off the question: when they come back to life we will work it out. Another version says: when משה רבינו comes with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: When they come to life, we will be wise about it. Some say he answered: When משה רבינו comes with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע does not give a ruling. He says the question can be settled when it actually happens. A second version says משה רבינו will be there to tell us the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first two questions, this one gets no clear rule. In the first version, we will be able to work it out then. In the איכא דאמרי version, משה רבינו, who will be among the revived, will tell us. Both versions agree that the question is left open for now.

keyTerms.meaning: We will become wise about it, meaning we will figure it out

phrases.english: He said to them: When they come to life, we will be wise about them.
There are those who say:
When Moshe our teacher comes with them.
phrases.notes: משה רבינו will come back to life with them and tell us the answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: לִכְשֶׁיִּחְיוּ נֶחְכַּם לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 by putting it off.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No ruling for now. It will be settled when the dead come back to life, or when משה רבינו comes with them.
steps.whatToRemember: Of the three questions of בורות, the first two get clear answers: a pillar of salt is not a dead body, and a living person is not טמא. The third, about the revived dead, is left for the future.

steps.title: How can a person become wise?
steps.stepSummary: A new set opens, three questions of דרך ארץ. The first is: what should a person do to become wise?
steps.simpleTranslation: Three matters of proper conduct. What should a person do to become wise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new set, three questions about how to live. The first asks what a person should do to become wise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier sets were about הלכה, אגדה and odd-sounding questions (בורות). This set is about practical living. All three questions of this set appear on this amud: becoming wise, becoming wealthy (step 23), and having sons (step 29).

keyTerms.meaning: Proper conduct and practical life matters

phrases.english: Three matters of proper conduct:
What should a person do to become wise?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דִּבְרֵי דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The questions of בורות are finished, and a new category of questions begins.

steps.title: Learn more, do business less
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers: spend more time sitting and learning, and less time in business.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: He should spend more time sitting in learning and less time in business.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives a practical answer. Spend more time in the בית מדרש and cut back on business.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wisdom comes from time and effort spent learning. Business takes away that time, so it should be kept small.

keyTerms.meaning: Increase sitting, meaning time spent learning in the בית מדרש
And reduce time spent in business

phrases.english: He said to them: He should increase his sitting,
phrases.notes: Sitting here means sitting and learning in the בית מדרש.

phrases.english: and decrease his business.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: יַרְבֶּה בִּישִׁיבָה, וִימַעֵט בִּסְחוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Learn more and do less business.

steps.title: Many tried that and it did not work
steps.stepSummary: The people of Alexandria push back: many people did exactly this and still did not become wise.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Many have done so, and it did not help them!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioners challenge רבי יהושע's answer from real life. Plenty of people learned a lot and did little business, and they still did not become wise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge shows that effort alone is not a guaranteed path to wisdom. Something more must be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And it did not help them

phrases.english: They said: Many have done so,
and it did not help them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: הַרְבֵּה עָשׂוּ כֵּן, וְלֹא הוֹעִיל לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's advice to learn more and do less business.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Experience shows that many followed this advice and did not become wise, so it cannot be the whole answer.

steps.title: Pray to the One Who owns wisdom
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע adds that one must ask for mercy from ה׳, to Whom wisdom belongs, as the פסוק says that ה׳ gives wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they should ask for mercy from the One Who owns wisdom, as it says: For ה׳ gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers the challenge. Wisdom belongs to ה׳, so a person must also pray to Him for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wisdom is a gift from ה׳, not only the result of hard work. The פסוק in משלי is the proof that ה׳ is the One Who gives wisdom.

keyTerms.meaning: They should ask for mercy, meaning pray

phrases.english: Rather, they should ask for mercy
from the One to Whom wisdom belongs,
as it says: "For ה׳ gives wisdom;
phrases.notes: משלי 2:6

phrases.english: from His mouth come knowledge and understanding."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יְבַקְּשׁוּ רַחֲמִים מִמִּי שֶׁהַחׇכְמָה שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a missing element to the original answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning more and doing less business is enough to become wise.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person must also pray to ה׳, because wisdom is His gift.

steps.title: רבי חייא's parable of the king's feast
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא compares this to a king who makes a feast for his servants and sends food from his own table to those he loves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: A parable of a human king who made a feast for his servants, and he sends some of what is in front of him to those he loves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא gives a משל to explain how ה׳ gives wisdom. Everyone at the feast gets food, but the king sends something special from his own plate to those he loves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the פסוק "from His mouth". Beyond what everyone gets, ה׳ sends wisdom from His own "table" to those He loves. That is why one should pray for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A king of flesh and blood, a human king

phrases.english: רבי חייא taught:
A parable of a human king
who made a feast for his servants,
and he sends to those he loves from what is in front of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: מָשָׁל לְמֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains with a משל the idea in step 19 that wisdom comes from ה׳'s "mouth".
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wisdom is like special food the King sends from His own table to those He loves.

steps.title: Why did he need to say learn more?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if prayer is the real path to wisdom, what was רבי יהושע teaching with his first advice to learn more?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the first answer added. If wisdom comes through prayer, why did רבי יהושע first say to learn more and do less business?
steps.deeperAnalysis: It can look as if the prayer answer replaced the learning answer. The גמרא checks whether the first piece of advice still matters.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? Asks what a statement adds

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
phrases.notes: If prayer is the key, what did the first advice to learn more add?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how steps 17 and 19 fit together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the advice to learn more adds, if wisdom comes through prayer.

steps.title: You need both learning and prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one without the other is not enough. Prayer without learning does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: That this without that is not enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both pieces of advice are needed. Prayer without learning will not bring wisdom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second answer did not cancel the first. It completed it. Learning and prayer together are the path to wisdom.

keyTerms.meaning: Without this, it is not enough

steps.whatToRemember: To become wise, a person must learn a lot and also pray to ה׳ for wisdom. Neither one works alone.
steps.confusionAlert: The prayer answer did not replace the learning answer. Both are needed together.

phrases.english: That this without that is not enough.
phrases.notes: "This" is prayer and "that" is sitting and learning.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא בְּלָא הָא לָא סַגִּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Prayer without learning is not enough, so both are needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a lasting lesson about עבודת ה׳: hard work in learning and prayer for help from Above go together.

steps.title: How Does a Person Become Wealthy?
steps.stepSummary: The people of Alexandria ask רבי יהושע what a person should do to become rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should a person do so that he becomes wealthy?
steps.whatsHappening: The people of Alexandria start a new question, this time about money instead of wisdom. This sets up רבי יהושע's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question is built exactly like the earlier one about wisdom. Seeing the same pattern helps us expect the same kind of answer: effort plus prayer.

phrases.english: What should a person do and become wealthy?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם וְיִתְעַשֵּׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second of the three דרך ארץ questions, following the same pattern as the wisdom question (Steps 16-22).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical steps lead a person to wealth?

steps.title: Do More Business, and Do It Honestly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers: spend more time in business and deal faithfully.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: he should do a lot of business and buy and sell honestly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives the practical answer: work hard at trade and be honest in your dealings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The advice has two parts. One is effort, doing more business. The other is honesty, dealing faithfully. This matches his first answer about wisdom, which was to learn more.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'take and give'; to do business, buy and sell

phrases.english: He said to them: He should increase in business,
and buy and sell faithfully.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: יַרְבֶּה בִּסְחוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Increase business activity and deal honestly.

steps.title: Many Tried This and It Didn't Work
steps.stepSummary: The people of Alexandria object that many people did business honestly and still did not become rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: many people did this, and it did not help them.
steps.whatsHappening: The people of Alexandria push back on רבי יהושע's advice using real life. Plenty of hard, honest workers stay poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge says that effort and honesty cannot be the full answer, because experience shows they do not always bring wealth. Something more must be needed.

phrases.english: They said to him: Many did so,
and it did not help!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הַרְבֵּה עָשׂוּ כֵּן, וְלֹא הוֹעִילוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the advice given in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's claim that honest, hard business leads to wealth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real experience: many followed this advice and stayed poor, so it cannot be enough.

steps.title: Pray to the One Who Owns All Wealth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע adds that one must ask ה׳ for mercy, because all silver and gold belong to Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he should ask for mercy from the One Who owns all wealth, as the פסוק says: 'Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers the challenge. Wealth really comes from ה׳, so a person must pray to Him for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hard work alone does not decide who becomes rich, because ה׳ owns all money and gives it to whom He wants. That explains why some honest workers stay poor: the missing part is תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: He should ask for mercy, pray
'Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold' (ה׳ is speaking)

phrases.english: Rather, he should ask for mercy
from the One to Whom wealth belongs,
phrases.notes: This means ה׳.

phrases.english: as it is said: "Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold."
phrases.notes: חגי 2:8

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים מִמִּי שֶׁהָעוֹשֶׁר שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 25 by adding prayer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a missing element (prayer) rather than taking back the earlier advice.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Business effort and honesty alone bring wealth.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wealth belongs to ה׳, so one must also pray to Him.

steps.title: Then Why Was the Business Advice Needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהושע's first advice adds if prayer is the real key.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question it asked about wisdom. If wealth comes from prayer, why did רבי יהושע first tell people to do business? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks whether the first advice now seems unnecessary. If the final answer is prayer, the advice about business looks like it has no purpose.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the role of Step 24 in light of Step 26, the same way Step 21 did for wisdom.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the first advice, to increase business honestly.

steps.title: Each One Needs the Other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that prayer without honest effort is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: That this without that is not enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that both parts are needed. A person must work honestly and also pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first advice was not cancelled. It is one half of the answer. Prayer does not replace effort, and effort does not replace prayer.
steps.whatToRemember: For wealth, just like for wisdom, a person needs both real honest effort and תפילה to ה׳. Neither one is enough alone.

phrases.english: that this without that is not enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא בְּלָא הָא לָא סַגִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 27 with the same principle given in Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both effort and prayer are required; one without the other does not suffice.

steps.title: How Does a Person Have Sons?
steps.stepSummary: The people of Alexandria ask what a person should do to have male children.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should a person do so that he will have sons?
steps.whatsHappening: The people of Alexandria move to a new question about having male children. This sets up רבי יהושע's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the third question in the series, after wisdom and wealth. It follows the same pattern, so we can expect advice about practical action and prayer.

phrases.english: What should a person do
so that he will have male children?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם וְיִהְיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים זְכָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question in the same series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical steps help a person have sons?

steps.title: Marry a Fitting Wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע begins his answer: a man should marry a woman who is fitting for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: he should marry a woman who is fitting for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע starts the practical part of his answer: marry a proper, suitable wife. The answer continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier answers, this begins with a practical action a person can take. The sentence is not finished here, and more of the answer follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is fitting or suitable for him

phrases.english: He said to them: He should marry a woman
who is fitting for him,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: יִשָּׂא אִשָּׁה הַהוֹגֶנֶת לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Marry a suitable wife (the answer continues past this point).
